title: A finite type algebra is locally quasi-finite over a polynomial algebra in its fibre dimension
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be prime, and let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be its inverse image. Write $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $\mathfrak Q=\ker(F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$ for the corresponding prime. Suppose the Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at $\mathfrak Q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is an integer $n\ge0$. Then there are $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ and an $R$-algebra homomorphism $R[t_1,\dots,t_n]\to S_g$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-ring-localization-away] which is quasi-finite: it is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $S_g$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].
